title: Fusion analysis overview
introduction: Gene fusions join sequences from previously independent genes, often through chromosomal inversions, deletions, or translocations. RNA sequencing can detect the resulting chimeric transcripts. Fusion analysis identifies candidate events and prioritizes them for review; a computational call alone does not establish biological or clinical significance.

workflow.title: Pipeline overview and core stages
workflow.introduction: A typical workflow moves from sequence quality assessment to alignment, candidate discovery, filtering, and interpretation. Misalignments, homologous sequences, sequencing errors, and transcripts spanning adjacent genes can complicate interpretation. Specific stages and filtering rules depend on the caller and its configuration.
rows: Pre-processing
Quality assessment and trimming
Assess read quality, for example with FastQC, and trim adapters or low-quality sequence when required using a trimming tool such as Trimmomatic.
Alignment
Read mapping
Map reads to a reference genome or transcriptome with an aligner suitable for the caller, such as STAR or Bowtie2.
Candidate discovery
Chimeric detection
Identify split reads spanning a fusion junction and discordant read pairs supporting a connection between the partner genes.
Assembly
Breakpoint sequence reconstruction
Some workflows use local de novo assembly to reconstruct candidate fusion sequences. This is not a universal step in all three callers.
Filtering
Artifact assessment
Evaluate homologous sequences, pseudogenes, ribosomal RNA, recurrent background events, and adjacent-gene read-through candidates according to the caller's rules.
Annotation
Functional interpretation
Assess reading frame, transcript context, and retained protein domains, including kinase domains when relevant.

items.label: Split reads
items.text: Individual reads span a candidate fusion junction: one portion aligns to one partner gene and the other portion to the second partner.

items.label: Discordant pairs or bridge reads
items.text: In paired-end sequencing, the two mates support different partner genes or an unexpected alignment configuration. These pairs support a candidate event but do not by themselves pinpoint the junction sequence.

items.label: Review of the evidence
items.text: Read support is evidence for prioritization, not proof of a true fusion. Review breakpoint alignments, mapping quality, sequence homology, reading frame, and caller-specific artifact annotations. Support metrics are defined differently by the three tools and should not be treated as directly interchangeable.

comparison.title: Comparison of the three callers
comparison.introduction: The supplied overview contrasts sensitivity, specificity, runtime, and filtering strategy. These are qualitative descriptions: performance depends on data quality, reference resources, software version, parameters, and computing environment. This report does not benchmark the tools or establish clinical suitability.

items.name: STAR-Fusion
items.description: STAR-Fusion uses chimeric alignment signals produced by STAR and fits into STAR/Trinity-related analysis workflows. The supplied overview highlights efficient processing and precision, while noting that complex rearrangements can be challenging.
items.strength: Reuse of compatible STAR alignment evidence and integration into larger RNA-seq workflows.
items.limitation: Sensitivity to difficult rearrangements, including some immunoglobulin-related events, depends on the data and configuration; compare caller outputs and inspect alignments.
items.report_ranking: Candidates in this report are ranked by junction-read count plus spanning-fragment count, then by junction reads and spanning fragments. Duplicate FusionName values are reduced to one row.

items.name: Arriba
items.description: Arriba was developed at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ). The supplied overview emphasizes sensitive detection in challenging samples and support for events such as viral integrations and internal tandem duplications.
items.strength: Detailed confidence and filter annotations help organize review of fusion candidates and complex events.
items.limitation: A high-confidence label is a caller classification, not a substitute for alignment review or independent validation. Biological background and mapping artifacts still require assessment.
items.report_ranking: Candidates in this report are ranked by confidence (high, medium, low), then summed split reads and discordant mates. Duplicate gene-pair names are reduced to one row.

items.name: FusionCatcher
items.description: FusionCatcher uses extensive reference information to annotate or filter candidates associated with artifacts, pseudogenes, homologous sequences, and fusions observed in normal samples. The supplied overview emphasizes its multi-step filtering approach.
items.strength: Rich filtering and annotation resources support investigation of potential background or artifactual calls.
items.limitation: Reference resources and multiple processing steps can require substantial disk space and runtime. Filtering does not guarantee that every retained candidate is a true fusion.
items.report_ranking: Rows are grouped by fusion pair. The maximum spanning-pair count and maximum unique-spanning-read count are retained for ranking, and descriptive annotations are combined. IGV coordinates come from the row with the highest spanning-pair count, then unique-read count.
